action_criteria.expected_evidence: Evans index 0.34 (0.26 two years earlier) with an acute callosal angle (88 degrees) and temporal horns enlarged out of proportion to the hippocampi (MTA 1); DESH incomplete; bilateral loss of the swallow-tail sign; no pontine, middle cerebellar peduncle or putaminal signal change; Fazekas grade 1; no obstructing lesion
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI for ventricular size, iNPH supportive features and an obstructing cause
action_criteria.rationale: A new wide-based magnetic gait and urge incontinence in her Parkinson's disease need an MRI that measures the ventricles against the scan of two years ago, looks for signs of multiple system atrophy and excludes obstruction before CSF is removed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sodium, creatinine, blood count, TSH and vitamin B12

action_criteria.rationale: A thyroid and B12 screen is reasonable for her slower thinking but does not decide the iNPH question.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: In the ON state: TUG 29 s, 10-metre walk 22 s in 31 steps, 180-degree turn in 8 steps, doorway freezing and retropulsion
action_criteria.label: Baseline timed gait assessment before the tap, in a defined medication state
action_criteria.rationale: Her ON-OFF cycles are predictable, so the baseline must be timed at a stated point after the levodopa dose for a tap response to be told apart from a dopaminergic effect.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MoCA 22/30 with visuospatial-executive, letter fluency and attention deficits and free recall 2/5 improving to 4/5 with cues

action_criteria.rationale: Her husband reports three months of forgetfulness and slowing, so a MoCA documents the profile and gives the tap a cognitive baseline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Opening pressure 18 cmH2O, normal cells, protein and glucose; 38 mL removed; in the ON state TUG 29 to 23 s at 24 hours (21%), 10-metre walk 22 to 16 s, MoCA 22 to 24
action_criteria.label: Lumbar tap test with opening pressure and CSF removal
action_criteria.rationale: Normal-pressure CSF and an objective tap response in an unchanged ON state identify the component of her decline that a shunt can treat.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: In the ON state: TUG 23 s at 24 hours (21% faster); 10-metre walk 16 s (27% faster); MoCA 24/30; tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia unchanged

action_criteria.rationale: Repeating the same timed measures at the same point after her levodopa dose shows that the gait improves while the parkinsonian signs do not.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform the large-volume lumbar tap before brain MRI has excluded a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus

Do not diagnose iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone: the diagnosis needs the clinical syndrome (gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms) and supportive imaging, with no other cause explaining them [Relkin_2005]
Do not withhold shunt referral solely because of Parkinson's disease
Do not attribute the accelerated gait decline and new urge incontinence to Parkinson's disease progression alone once ventriculomegaly with supportive features and a tap response are documented

Do not give dopamine-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol) for post-puncture or post-operative nausea or confusion in this patient with Parkinson's disease
required_recommendations: Refer to neurosurgery for CSF shunting with a programmable valve, on the basis of the tap-test improvement of 21% in TUG at 24 hours in the ON state, the supportive MRI (Evans index 0.34, up from 0.26 two years earlier, acute callosal angle, enlarged temporal horns) and normal-pressure CSF [Nakajima_2021]

Counsel that shunting is expected to improve the wide-based magnetic gait and urge incontinence more than the bradykinesia, rigidity and tremor, and that Parkinson's disease continues to need its own treatment [Nakajima_2021]
Continue carbidopa-levodopa unchanged and perform the pre- and post-tap gait measures in the same medication state, so the tap response is not confounded by a dopaminergic ON/OFF change
Review pramipexole as a contributor to confusion and falls, tapering it rather than stopping it abruptly if it is reduced
Falls-prevention measures (physiotherapy, home assessment, walking aid) while awaiting surgery

avoided_actions.rationale: She has no fluctuating awareness or episodes suggesting seizures, so an EEG cannot separate iNPH from its mimics.
Her falls come from freezing and impaired postural reflexes, without syncope or lightheadedness, so an ECG does not inform the gait work-up.
There is no syncope, murmur or embolic event, so echocardiography has no role in this work-up.
An MRI is available and shows the callosal angle, temporal horns, nigral signal and brainstem, which CT cannot.
There is no syncope and no orthostatic drop, so rhythm monitoring has no diagnostic role here.

DaTscan or other molecular imaging does not change the decision: her Parkinson's disease is clinically established, a DaTscan cannot separate it from multiple system atrophy, and the iNPH decision rests on MRI and the tap test.
A full neuropsychological battery is not needed for the iNPH decision; the bedside screen and timed gait measures are
Normal-pressure CSF with a normal cell count in a four-month afebrile gait syndrome gives no indication for prion, inflammatory or infectious assays.

accepted: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus with concurrent Parkinson's disease (NPH-PD copathology)

differential.diagnosis: Parkinson's disease progression / Parkinson's disease dementia
differential.key_features: Parkinson's disease is present and named in the diagnosis, but progression alone does not explain the new wide-based magnetic gait, ventricles enlarging from Evans index 0.26 to 0.34 or a 21% TUG improvement after CSF removal in an unchanged ON state.

differential.diagnosis: Atypical parkinsonism (multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy)
differential.key_features: The new incontinence and falls raise it, but there is no orthostatic drop, no retention, no cerebellar signs, full vertical saccades, a sustained levodopa response and a normal midbrain, pons, middle cerebellar peduncles and putamina on MRI.

differential.diagnosis: Adverse effect of dopamine agonist (pramipexole) on cognition and falls
differential.key_features: The dose has been unchanged for two years and she has no hallucinations or sleep attacks; the drug may add to the confusion but does not explain the ventricular enlargement or the tap response.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: White matter change is only Fazekas grade 1, too little to explain the decline.
Free recall improves from 2/5 to 4/5 with cues, the hippocampi are MTA 1 and the deficits are executive and attentional, which does not suggest Alzheimer's disease.

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventricles enlarging out of proportion to the sulci over two years, an acute callosal angle, temporal horns out of proportion to the hippocampi and a tap response argue against atrophy ex vacuo.
There is no history of head injury, subarachnoid haemorrhage, meningitis or intracranial surgery.

key_clinical_evidence: Four years into levodopa-responsive Parkinson's disease, four months of progression with a new wide-based magnetic gait, falls in the ON state, urge incontinence and cognitive slowing are out of proportion to her Hoehn-Yahr stage 2 disease and meet the clinical criteria for iNPH [Relkin_2005]

MRI shows Evans index 0.34, up from 0.26 two years earlier, with an acute callosal angle (88 degrees) and temporal horns enlarged out of proportion to the hippocampi; DESH is incomplete; the SWI swallow-tail loss fits the known Parkinson's disease [Nakajima_2021]

With baseline and post-tap measures in the same ON state, TUG improved 21% at 24 hours (29 to 23 s) and the 10-metre walk 27% (22 to 16 s), with fewer urgency episodes and unchanged tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia [Nakajima_2021]

No orthostatic hypotension, no urinary retention, no cerebellar signs, full saccades and a normal brainstem and putamina on MRI argue against multiple system atrophy or progressive supranuclear palsy as the cause of the new incontinence and falls
iNPH coexists with Parkinson's disease more often than chance; the copathology lowers the expected benefit of a shunt but does not exclude it, and the benefit is mainly for gait [Nakajima_2021]
Tap-test sensitivity is 26% to 61% with a PPV of 73% to 100% [Marmarou_2005]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The new wide-based magnetic gait and urge incontinence, ventricles enlarging to Evans index 0.34 with an acute callosal angle and enlarged temporal horns, and a 21% TUG improvement in an unchanged ON state identify a treatable iNPH component beside the Parkinson's disease.

sequence_constraints.reason: Brain imaging must exclude a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus before CSF is removed [Relkin_2005]

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait decline with falls, new urinary incontinence and slower thinking over four months in a woman with Parkinson's disease

patient.history_present_illness: A 72-year-old right-handed retired teacher with Parkinson's disease (diagnosed 4 years ago, Hoehn-Yahr stage 2 at her last clinic visit 6 months ago) was admitted after her movement disorder neurologist noted a change in her trajectory. She had been stably managed on carbidopa-levodopa and pramipexole, with good motor control and predictable ON-OFF cycles, and her mild right-hand resting tremor, bradykinesia and cogwheel rigidity were well controlled at that visit. Over the past four months her gait has progressively worsened in a way her neurologist describes as atypical for her stage: it is now wide-based, with reduced step height and a feet-stuck-to-the-floor quality. She has fallen several times despite being in her levodopa ON state. Freezing in doorways and narrow spaces did not improve with a trial of an additional daily carbidopa-levodopa dose, which was withdrawn; the pramipexole dose has been unchanged for two years. Urinary urgency with urge incontinence began two months ago, without hesitancy or a sense of incomplete emptying. Her husband reports that she has become more forgetful and slower in her thinking over the past three months. She has had no hallucinations, daytime sleep attacks, lightheadedness on standing or syncope, and no head injury, meningitis or intracranial haemorrhage. An MRI 2 years ago was reported as showing normal ventricular size (Evans index 0.26). A brain MRI obtained recently by her neurologist was reported as showing enlarged ventricles; the images are not available. She was admitted to determine whether a second process is contributing to the decline.

neurological_exam.gait: Examined about 1 hour after the morning levodopa dose (ON state). Hybrid gait: parkinsonian features (reduced arm swing, bradykinesia) combined with a wide base, reduced step height and a magnetic quality; en-bloc turning; freezing at the doorway even in the ON state.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, attentive, oriented to person and place but not to date; slowed responses. No aphasia. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral cogwheel rigidity (right > left). Mild resting tremor of the right hand, 3-4 Hz. Bradykinesia of both upper limbs, right more than left. Strength 5/5 throughout.
